Decoding the Human Brain

NeuroHINTS Labs — Human Intracranial Neurophysiology, NeuroTechnology, and Stimulation

The NeuroHINTS Labs (Human Intracranial Neurophysiology, Neurotechnology, and Stimulation) are a collaborative, team-based research enterprise focused on bringing together experts to understand brain function under normal and pathological conditions. We aim to develop advanced techniques for diagnosing and treating devastating neuropsychiatric diseases.

We focus on using approaches which extract information at multiple scales and then combine them into a more complete and meaningful understanding of brain physiology; our research allows us to design therapeutic interventions including brain-computer (machine) neuroprosthetics. To reach these goals we are actively developing new methods (neurotechnology & AI) for measuring and modulating neural activity in the brain and using sophisticated signal processing and machine learning techniques to better understand complex neural signals. We are a founding lab of the Clinical Data Animation Center (CDAC) and the Center for Neurotechnology and Neurorecovery (CNTR). We are also part of the consortium of labs involved in the BrainGate Clinical Trial.

Interdisciplinary Science & Group Identities

Research Groups & Specialized Teams

The NeuroHINTS Labs are organized into specialized research groups and five collaborative teams. Together, we integrate single-neuron and intracranial electrophysiology, neural engineering, clinical neurology, oncology, and artificial intelligence to decode and modulate the human brain.

Interdisciplinary Science & Group Identities

Research Groups & Specialized Teams

The NeuroHINTS Labs are organized into specialized research groups and five collaborative teams. Together, we integrate single-neuron and intracranial electrophysiology, neural engineering, clinical neurology, oncology, and artificial intelligence to decode and modulate the human brain.

Epilepsy & Neuromodulation Team

Seizure Dynamics, Biomarkers & Direct Brain Stimulation

Investigating how seizures initiate, propagate, and terminate across micro- and macro-scales, and using targeted electrical stimulation to disrupt epileptogenic networks.

1. Seizure Onset & Termination Dynamics

Classifying electrophysiological seizure onset patterns and identifying universal network state transitions that govern how seizures self-terminate.

2. Micro-Scale Biomarkers & HFOs

Using hybrid macro/micro depth electrodes and high-density grids to map pathological ripples, fast ripples, and single-unit firing within the seizure onset zone.

3. Brain Connectivity & Stimulation Mapping

Probing effective network excitability with single-pulse electrical stimulation (SPES) and cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) across brain states.

4. Closed-Loop Therapeutic Neuromodulation

Developing real-time biomarker-triggered cortical and subcortical stimulation protocols to suppress ictal synchronization and restore physiological rhythms.

Cognition & Sleep Team

Sleep Oscillations, Memory Consolidation & Cognitive Control

Recording directly from the human cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus to decode how sleep oscillations coordinate memory consolidation and how stimulation modulates cognition.

1. Slow Waves, Spindles & Hippocampal Ripples

Mapping the precise temporal coupling between cortical slow oscillations, thalamic spindles, and hippocampal sharp-wave ripples during human NREM sleep.

2. Memory, Language & NeuroEconomics

Tracking single-unit ensembles and local field potentials during working memory, semantic processing, decision-making (NeuroEconomics), and overnight memory consolidation.

3. Closed-Loop Stimulation for Cognitive Enhancement

Delivering phase-locked intracranial stimulation synchronized to endogenous oscillations to causal-test and enhance memory encoding and emotional regulation.

4. Interplay Between Sleep Architecture & Epilepsy

Dissecting how interictal epileptiform discharges hijack physiological sleep oscillations and impair memory consolidation in patients with epilepsy.

Neurotechnology Team

High-Density Human Neural Interfaces & Closed-Loop Systems

Pioneering ultra-high-resolution recording arrays and real-time closed-loop stimulation platforms for translational human neurophysiology in the operating room and EMU.

1. Intraoperative Human Neuropixels Recordings

Resolving hundreds of simultaneous single neurons across human cortical laminae in vivo using high-density silicon Neuropixels probes.

2. Thin-Film Micro-ECoG (PtNRGrids & PEDOT:PSS)

Translating conformable thousand-channel platinum nanorod and organic polymer micro-electrocorticography grids to map sub-millimeter cortical dynamics.

3. CLoSES Real-Time Closed-Loop Stimulation

Engineering open-source hardware/software pipelines that detect neural features with millisecond latency to trigger state-dependent intracranial stimulation.

4. Biophysics of Direct Human Brain Stimulation

Quantifying how stimulation frequency, amplitude, pulse width, and electrode geometry shape local and distant cortical evoked responses.

Cancer Neuroscience (Paulk & Hadar Labs)

Tumor-Induced Network Hyperexcitability & Glioma Circuits

Bridging neuro-oncology and human systems neurophysiology to uncover how primary and metastatic brain tumors remodel surrounding human cortical circuits.

1. Intraoperative High-Density Recordings in Glioma

Deploying micro-ECoG and laminar probes during awake craniotomies to map single-neuron and local field potential hyperexcitability at the tumor-brain margin.

2. Cellular & Network Mechanisms of Tumor-Related Epilepsy

Investigating bidirectional synaptic and paracrine signaling between infiltrative glioma cells and peritumoral human cortical neurons.

AI in Neurology and Neuroscience of AI (Hadar Lab)

Epilepsy Therapeutics, AI, Mechanistic Interpretability & NeuroEconomics

Led by Dr. Peter Hadar, MD, MSc, developing deep learning models for neurophysiological biomarker discovery, mechanistic interpretability & representation engineering, investigating the neural basis of decision-making (NeuroEconomics), and evaluating Large Language Models for precision epilepsy therapeutics.

1. Deep Learning on Scalp & Intracranial EEG

Training self-supervised neural networks on large-scale sleep and EMU recordings to detect subtle signatures of epileptogenesis and treatment response.

2. Epilepsy Therapeutics, NeuroEconomics & Clinical LLMs

Investigating neural mechanisms of value and decision-making while extracting longitudinal seizure outcomes and anti-seizure medication responses via Large Language Models.

Cash Lab • Founding Director

Dr. Sydney Cash, MD, PhD

Division Chief of MGB Epilepsy & Neurophysiology • Professor of Neurology, HMS

Dr. Sydney Cash is the Division Chief of the Mass General Brigham Neurology Division of Epilepsy and Neurophysiology and Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School. He is the founding director of the NeuroHINTS Labs and co-director of the Center for Neurotechnology and Neurorecovery (CNTR). His work focuses on understanding human brain physiology at multiple scales, from single neurons to large-scale networks, particularly in the contexts of epilepsy, sleep, and cognition.

Paulk Lab

Dr. Angelique Paulk, Ph.D.

Assistant Professor of Neurology, Harvard Medical School • MGH

Dr. Angelique Paulk is an Assistant Professor with a background in systems neuroscience. She investigates how human brain circuits process information and respond to direct electrical stimulation using advanced microelectrodes including Neuropixels and PtNRGrids. She also leads an NIH-funded research effort in Cancer Neuroscience, studying how brain tumors interact with and alter surrounding neural networks.

Salami Lab

Dr. Pariya Salami, Ph.D.

Instructor in Neurology, Harvard Medical School • MGH

Dr. Pariya Salami is an Instructor whose research focuses on neurophysiology, EEG, and computational signal processing. She uses intracranial recordings in patients with epilepsy to study how seizures start, spread, and terminate, and how surrounding brain states influence seizure dynamics.

Zelmann Lab

Dr. Rina Zelmann, Ph.D.

Assistant Professor of Neurology, Harvard Medical School • MGH

Dr. Rina Zelmann is an Assistant Professor working at the intersection of biomedical engineering and clinical neuroscience. She specializes in intracranial EEG analysis, high-frequency oscillations, and closed-loop stimulation (CLoSES), with a focus on modulating brain networks involved in epilepsy, sleep, and cognition.

Hadar Lab • Epilepsy Therapeutics, AI, NeuroEconomics

Dr. Peter Hadar, MD, MSc

Instructor in Neurology, HMS • MGH • BWH

Dr. Peter Hadar, MD, MSc (Instructor in Neurology, HMS • MGH • BWH) leads the Hadar Lab in Epilepsy Therapeutics, AI, and NeuroEconomics, applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, mechanistic interpretability, and decision science to clinical neurophysiology and medical text. His projects include using deep learning on sleep and clinical EEG to improve epilepsy diagnosis, investigating the neural mechanisms of decision-making (NeuroEconomics), and leveraging Large Language Models to extract clinically meaningful insights from electronic health records.
